findings.issue: The live cw8 never exercises the child second measurement on a healthy reading: the re-measurement is only taken when a last step is over WIDE_STEP, which a linear reading does not reach. Deleting the again() closure, or dropping the again field from the child output, leaves cw8 green and every pure case (cw17, cw21-cw23) green too, because they call the pure helpers and never the child. Only the executor probe rows (WIDE_STEP lowered to 0.5) catch the wiring, and a probe is not part of the suite.
findings.resolution: Let the job carry the step (job step, defaulting to WIDE_STEP) and add one permanent case that runs the child with the step at 0.5 and asserts the output holds an again entry with two seconds for every kind. That puts the wiring the probe proves under a case that fails when it is deleted.

findings.issue: cw8 is not at least as strict as before SG2.23 narrowed it, and the filed outcome sentence that everything cw8 caught before still fails overclaims if before means the per-step judgement. That judgement flagged any step over 2 ** 1.5 (about 2.83x); the new one flags only the LAST step, only above 3.5x, only when a second measurement also exceeds it. A middle step of 4x with a linear tail, or a last step between 2.83x and 3.5x, was red before SG2.23 and is green now. That is what the task RULE asked for (a bound between the 3.00x CI recorded and a quadratic 4x), so it is not a defect in the diff, but the outcome should say so.
findings.resolution: State in the outcome that cw8 is restored for the quadratic last doubling the task names and stays narrower than the pre-SG2.23 per-step bound for middle steps and for last steps in 2.83x-3.5x; no code change needed.

intent.note: Task clause (1): co2 again holds the whole list: the lines that name skills are exactly [- from-plan], the lead line is first, and the two ask lines follow the names and are the last two lines. The diff asserts len(listed) >= 4, listed[0] is not a dash line and holds Skill tool, the dash lines are exactly [- from-plan], listed[1:-2] == [- from-plan] (which with the other clauses fixes the length at exactly four), listed[-2] holds skillsInvoked and listed[-1] holds skillUnavailable. The ask lines are identified by those field names, which the task allowed and the outcome says. Against b16a5c49 parent (listed[1:] == [- from-plan], a two-line list) the new co2 rejects every list the old one rejected except the one the plan now produces, so it is at least as strict; the old check never named the asks, the new one does. Clause (2): a last step over a per-step bound is MEASURED AGAIN in the same child, the last two lengths only, fresh rounds; the kind is red only when the re-measured step is also over the bound; give the pure judgement the re-measured step as an input. The diff adds WIDE_STEP = 3.5 (between 3.00x and 4x, reasoned in the comment), last_step_again (calls measure() only when the last step is over the bound), _last_step_faults, and an elif in _run_faults reading run[again]; the child calls growth_series again over units[-2:] with the series deadline remainder, and the slope is unchanged. Cases: (2,2,4) re-measured at 4 is red with one sentence naming the last doubling (cw21), re-measured at 2 is green (cw21), cw17 series stay green and cw18 stay red, a step at or under the bound is never re-measured with calls counted (cw23), plus the bound twins (cw22). The executor claim describes the diff accurately except the overclaim in finding 2. The floor guard one finding (co2 label changed, so it reads as gone) is the intended rewording of a case that became stricter; its not-compared file tests/test__clause_coverage.py I read: outside the new elif in _run_faults, the child and the helpers, the diff touches only comments, the cw17 fixture, the cw8 label and the new cases, and removes no check. The unrelated .claude/.gitignore edit is in the working tree but outside the task scope and diff. On false reds: any run the new last-step judgement reds, the pre-SG2 per-step judgement also reds (a last step over 3.5x is over 2.83x), so it is never noisier than before SG2; against the slope-only state it adds a red only when a last step over 3.5x is confirmed by a fresh two-length measurement over 3.5x, and the CI-recorded 2.92x and 3.00x never reach the second measurement. Residual risk: a noise burst long enough to cover both measurements, or a systematic step (cache boundary) over 3.5x, which would repeat.
